title: The Magnifying Lens
mechanism: Lens optics: a broken lens that makes print look bigger is a converging (far-sighted) lens, and such glasses also make the wearer's eyes look bigger; near-sighted lenses shrink the eyes, sunglasses do not magnify.
false_lead: Hugo argued with the victim and wears thick glasses

seg.hook: A broken lens at a murder scene. It can only belong to one pair of eyes.
seg.case: An antiques dealer is found dead. Under his desk, a shard of a broken glasses lens. Hold it over a newspaper, and the letters look bigger.
seg.s1: Hugo, his rival, wears thick glasses that make his eyes look tiny. "We argued, yes. That's all."
seg.s2: Greta, the bookkeeper, wears glasses that make her eyes look huge. "I left at six."
seg.s3: Felix, the nephew, wears plain dark sunglasses. "I was never here."
seg.challenge: Who killed the dealer? You have five seconds. Five. Four. Three. Two. One.
seg.reveal: It was Greta. A magnifying lens is for far-sighted eyes, and it makes the wearer's eyes look bigger too. Hugo's lenses shrink. Sunglasses don't magnify. Hugo's argument was a false lead.
seg.outro: Did you solve it? Comment your answer. This is ClueLab.

title: The Dry Umbrella
mechanism: Weather timeline: a downpour from 8 PM means anyone arriving at 9 must have a wet umbrella and shoes; a bone-dry, still-strapped umbrella proves the guest was inside before the rain, during the theft.
false_lead: Kara arrived early, before the theft

seg.hook: Three guests. Three umbrellas. One of them never saw the rain.
seg.case: A villa dinner party. At eight sharp, a downpour begins and lasts all night. At eight thirty, a necklace vanishes from upstairs.
seg.s1: Ines: "I arrived at nine." Her umbrella is dripping, her shoes soaked.
seg.s2: Jonah: "I arrived at nine too." His umbrella is bone dry, still strapped shut. His shoes are dry.
seg.s3: Kara: "I came at seven thirty, to help the cook." The cook says she never left the kitchen.
seg.challenge: Who stole the necklace? You have five seconds. Five. Four. Three. Two. One.
seg.reveal: It was Jonah. Anyone arriving at nine walked through an hour of pouring rain. His dry umbrella and shoes mean he was inside before eight. Kara came early, but the cook vouches for her.
seg.outro: Did you solve it? Comment your answer. This is ClueLab.

title: The Parrot's Ringtone
mechanism: Parrot mimicry: a parrot only learns sounds it hears repeatedly, so its newly copied ringtone proves the phone's owner has been in the house many times, contradicting a claimed single visit a year ago.
false_lead: Mara has a key to the house

seg.hook: The only witness to this theft has feathers. And it's still talking.
seg.case: Mrs. Vale's jewels vanish, one piece at a time, over several weeks. Her parrot, Captain, copies any sound he hears again and again. Lately, he chirps a new one: three rising notes, then a ding.
seg.s1: Leo, the gardener, comes every day. His phone rings like an old bell.
seg.s2: Mara, the niece, has a key. Her phone is always on silent.
seg.s3: Noah, the piano tuner: "I was here once, a year ago." His ringtone: three rising notes, then a ding.
seg.challenge: Who stole the jewels? You have five seconds. Five. Four. Three. Two. One.
seg.reveal: It was Noah. A parrot only learns a sound it hears over and over. Captain learned Noah's ringtone, so Noah has been there many times. Mara's key was a false lead.
seg.outro: Did you solve it? Comment your answer. This is ClueLab.

title: The Poisoned Envelope
mechanism: Poison on envelope glue: a prepaid return envelope with poisoned gum kills the recipient when he licks it shut, so the killer never comes near the locked room.
false_lead: Ruth cooked his dinner and made his tea

seg.hook: He died alone, behind a locked door. The killer was miles away.
seg.case: Professor Lund is found dead at his desk, the door locked. Poison on his tongue, but his food and tea are clean. Beside him, one envelope, freshly sealed.
seg.s1: Ruth, the housekeeper, cooked his dinner and made his tea.
seg.s2: Simon, his business partner, mailed him a contract with a return envelope: "Sign it and send it back today."
seg.s3: Tara, his student, emailed him her thesis that morning.
seg.challenge: Who poisoned the professor? You have five seconds. Five. Four. Three. Two. One.
seg.reveal: It was Simon. The poison was on the glue of his return envelope. When Lund licked it to seal it, he poisoned himself. Simon never came near him. Ruth's cooking was a false lead.
seg.outro: Did you solve it? Comment your answer. This is ClueLab.

title: The Running Stride
mechanism: Gait analysis in sand: running leaves long gaps between steps and toe-only impressions; walking leaves short steps and full prints; a heavy load only deepens prints.
false_lead: Yara's deep prints and heavy bag

seg.hook: Three trails of footprints in the sand. Only one of them was running.
seg.case: A beach hut is broken into at sunset. The thief flees across the wet sand. Three trails of prints lead away, each matching one suspect's shoes.
seg.s1: Vera: "I walked my dog." Short, even steps, with paw prints beside them.
seg.s2: Wim: "I strolled slowly, watching the sunset." Steps two meters apart. Deep toes, almost no heels.
seg.s3: Yara: "I carried a heavy bag home." Short steps, every print pressed deep.
seg.challenge: Who fled from the hut? You have five seconds. Five. Four. Three. Two. One.
seg.reveal: It was Wim. Long gaps and only the toes digging in: that is how a runner's feet land. A stroll leaves short steps and full prints. Yara's heavy bag only made her prints deeper. A false lead.
seg.outro: Did you solve it? Comment your answer. This is ClueLab.

title: The Camera That Wasn't
mechanism: Bluffed evidence: told of a non-existent camera, the guilty one pre-emptively amends his story to explain footage that cannot exist; innocent people have nothing to explain.

seg.hook: The detective told one lie. It made the thief tell the truth.
seg.case: Cash vanishes from a warehouse office at ten at night. Basil holds the cash-box key. The detective tells the staff: "There's a camera over the back door. We get the footage tomorrow." There is no camera.
seg.s2: Corinne: "Fine. You'll see I left by the front."
seg.s3: Dmitri, an hour later: "Oh, I forgot. I did step out the back door around ten. For a smoke. Just so you know."
seg.challenge: Who took the cash? You have five seconds. Five. Four. Three. Two. One.
seg.reveal: It was Dmitri. The camera doesn't exist, so it can't show anyone. Only the guilty man feared what it would show, and rushed to explain himself in advance. Basil's key was a false lead.
seg.outro: Did you solve it? Comment your answer. This is ClueLab.

title: The Last Heartbeat
mechanism: Wearable time of death: a smartwatch heart-rate log fixes death at 10:17 PM, overriding the doctor's 9 PM estimate and breaking an alibi that only covers 9 PM.

seg.hook: The doctor said he died at nine. His watch disagrees.
seg.case: Mr. Hale is found dead in his flat. The doctor guesses he died around nine. But his smartwatch logged his heart: calm all evening, racing at ten fourteen, then zero at ten seventeen.
seg.s1: Elsa paid a restaurant bill at ten twelve, thirty minutes' drive away.
seg.s2: Finn was streaming live online until eleven. Then he found the body.
seg.s3: Gil: "I was with friends from eight thirty to nine thirty. Then home, alone."
seg.challenge: Who killed Mr. Hale? You have five seconds. Five. Four. Three. Two. One.
seg.reveal: It was Gil. The watch proves Hale died at ten seventeen, not nine. Gil's alibi covers nine, but not ten. Elsa was across town, and Finn was live online. Finding the body was a false lead.
seg.outro: Did you solve it? Comment your answer. This is ClueLab.

title: The Noon Rainbow
mechanism: Rainbow geometry: a rainbow only forms when the sun is low (below about 42 degrees), so a rainbow under a high midsummer noon sun is impossible.
tags: at her desk, boss saw her

seg.hook: One alibi includes a rainbow. That's exactly what gives it away.
seg.case: Midsummer. At twelve noon, a painting is stolen from the city museum, while a summer shower passes over town. Remember: a rainbow can only appear when the sun is low in the sky.
seg.s1: Hana: "At noon I was in a café, watching the rain."
seg.s2: Ivan: "At noon I was hiking. The sun was right above me, and I saw a huge rainbow."
seg.s3: Juno, who has a museum pass: "At noon I was at my desk. My boss saw me."
seg.challenge: Who stole the painting? You have five seconds. Five. Four. Three. Two. One.
seg.reveal: It was Ivan. At midsummer noon, the sun is far too high for a rainbow to form. He invented a pretty detail and gave himself away. Hana's story fits the shower. Juno's pass was a false lead.
seg.outro: Did you solve it? Comment your answer. This is ClueLab.

title: The Price Sticker
mechanism: Replaced footwear: soles claimed to be years old but spotless with a shop price sticker prove the shoes were bought after the crime to replace the pair that left the print.
false_lead: Tess's boots are caked in flowerbed mud

seg.hook: He swore he'd worn these shoes for years. Look at the soles.
seg.case: A villa is burgled at night. In the flowerbed under the window, a clear shoe print: size forty-three trainers. Police check three suspects with that size.
seg.s1: Rafe's trainers are well worn, but with a different tread pattern.
seg.s2: Sami: "These are my only shoes. I've had them for years." The soles are spotless, with a price sticker still on one.
seg.s3: Tess, the gardener, wears boots caked in flowerbed mud.
seg.challenge: Who burgled the villa? You have five seconds. Five. Four. Three. Two. One.
seg.reveal: It was Sami. Years of walking leave soles scuffed and dirty. A price sticker means they were bought yesterday, to replace the pair that left the print. Tess's muddy boots were a false lead.
seg.outro: Did you solve it? Comment your answer. This is ClueLab.

title: The Letterbox Hook
mechanism: Letterbox fishing: keys on a hook near the front door are lifted out through the letterbox with a telescopic rod and hook, so a locked house is robbed without entry; the rod scratches the flap.
false_lead: Abel has a spare house key

seg.hook: No key. No broken window. No way in. And yet, the car keys are gone.
seg.case: At dawn, Mr. Doyle's car is stolen. His house is locked, no window broken. The keys hung on a hook one meter inside the front door. Fresh scratches line the inside of the letterbox.
seg.s1: Abel, his brother, has a spare house key: "I was asleep at home."
seg.s2: Bree, his neighbor, borrowed the car last week: "I gave the keys back."
seg.s3: Cyril walked past the house that night, carrying his long telescopic fishing rod.
seg.challenge: Who stole the car? You have five seconds. Five. Four. Three. Two. One.
seg.reveal: It was Cyril. Nobody went inside. A telescopic rod with a hook, slipped through the letterbox, lifts keys off a hook a meter away, and scratches the flap. A spare key scratches nothing. Abel was a false lead.
seg.outro: Did you solve it? Comment your answer. This is ClueLab.

title: The Chalk Line
mechanism: Tyre chalk rotation: a warden's chalk line on top of a tyre only moves if the wheel turns, so a mark rotated to the bottom proves the car left and was re-parked in the same spot.
board: 9 AM: CHALK ON TOP OF TYRES

seg.hook: Three cars that never moved. A single chalk line says one of them did.
seg.case: At nine, a traffic warden chalks a line on the top of every parked car's front tyre. At ten, a jeweller's across town is robbed. At eleven, police check three cars.
seg.s1: Dana: "My car hasn't moved since eight." The chalk line is right at the top.
seg.s2: Eli: "Mine neither." Chalk at the top too, and a fresh dent in the bumper.
seg.s3: Faye: "Mine hasn't moved either." Same spot. But her chalk line is at the bottom, touching the road.
seg.challenge: Who drove to the robbery? You have five seconds. Five. Four. Three. Two. One.
seg.reveal: It was Faye. A chalk line can only move if the wheel turns. Hers rolled to the bottom: she drove off and parked back in the same spot. Eli's dent was a false lead.
seg.outro: Did you solve it? Comment your answer. This is ClueLab.

title: The Past Tense
mechanism: Verb-tense slip: while a person is only missing, everyone speaks of her in the present tense; the one who knows she is dead slips into the past tense.
false_lead: The husband raised her life insurance

seg.hook: She's only missing. So why does one of them talk about her as if she's gone?
seg.case: Lena Ross has been missing for two days. No body. No note. Her husband recently raised her life insurance. The detective asks three people about her.
seg.s1: Max, her husband: "She is the kindest person I know. Please, bring her home."
seg.s2: Nell, her sister: "She's stubborn. She'll turn up. She always does."
seg.s3: Pierce, her business partner: "Lena was brilliant. She was always the first in the office."
seg.challenge: Who knows what happened to Lena? You have five seconds. Five. Four. Three. Two. One.
seg.reveal: It was Pierce. Everyone else still speaks about Lena in the present tense. Only someone who knows she is dead slips into the past. The life insurance was a false lead.
seg.outro: Did you solve it? Comment your answer. This is ClueLab.
